subject.title: Control UI fails to load on Firefox desktop behind reverse proxy — CSP blocks Vite runtime eval(), 'Control UI did not start', WebSocket 1006

question: Should this issue stay separate for Firefox reverse-proxy WebSocket proof while the shared CSP/Zod work remains on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78362, and should unsafe-eval remain rejected as the default repair?
rationale: Source inspection supports the CSP/Zod problem, but automation cannot safely choose a CSP relaxation or decide whether the reverse-proxy 1006 symptom is the same root cause without live browser proof and maintainer security intent.

options.title: Keep Separate and Preserve Strict CSP
options.body: Keep this issue open for Firefox reverse-proxy proof while fixing the no-eval Zod path under the related CSP thread.

options.title: Fold Into CSP Thread
options.body: Treat the WebSocket failure as likely startup fallout from the CSP issue and consolidate the remaining work under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78362.

options.title: Accept CSP Relaxation
options.body: Allow unsafe-eval only if maintainers explicitly accept the broader Control UI script-execution risk and require upgrade/browser proof.

recommendation.title: Keep Separate and Preserve Strict CSP
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for Firefox reverse-proxy proof while fixing the no-eval Zod path under the related CSP thread.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across Control UI CSP, Gateway origin hardening, and reverse-proxy security behavior.
